en: Mount Mayon in the Philippines is famous for its perfect conical shape and frequent, hazardous volcanic eruptions.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of thousands of limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River demonstrates the water cycle by collecting rainfall and channeling it directly into the sea.
Nutrient-rich volcanic ash from Taal Volcano created highly fertile soil for agriculture in the surrounding Batangas region.
The Habagat, or southwest monsoon, brings heavy rainfall and causes flooding in the Philippines during the rainy season.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a massive, persistent anticyclonic storm that is larger than the planet Earth.
Sirius, also known as the Dog Star, is the brightest star visible in the Earth's night sky.
The Apollo 11 astronauts landed on the Moon's Sea of Tranquility, a large, dark basaltic plain.
The province of Romblon in the Philippines is widely known for mining and producing high-quality white marble.
Mount Apo features a tropical rainforest climate, characterized by high rainfall and consistently warm temperatures year-round.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo was the second-largest volcanic eruption of the twentieth century.
Super Typhoon Yolanda, known internationally as Haiyan, was one of the most powerful tropical cyclones ever recorded.
